summary: Feed s136_double to APM is degraded: 69.4% of TCP sessions are one-way (APM requires bidirectional visibility) and 8.0% duplicate packets detected. No drops, overload, VLAN or encryption issues found.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of traffic is reaching the APM, likely due to TAP/SPAN placement monitoring a single link direction or asymmetric routing where return path is not tapped, or packet broker policy splitting forward/return flows to different tool ports without bidirectional aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs both directions to correlate requests/responses and measure latency; with 111 of 160 sessions one-way it cannot compute response times, will produce incomplete traces and miss performance errors.

recommended_fix.why: Ensure forward and return packets for each session are aggregated to the same APM tool port so bidirectional transaction correlation works

findings.root_cause: 8.0% duplicates (148 of 1850 packets) indicates same packets delivered twice, typically from aggregating two SPAN/TAP feeds that see the same traffic or a packet broker forwarding loop without deduplication enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: Duplicates inflate APM transaction counts, distort latency and retransmission metrics, and waste tool capacity on the 10G port, causing false performance alerts.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication to deliver each packet once so APM metrics are accurate and capacity is not wasted
